items.exact_passage: The paper compares simulated size distributions with a fitted lognormal alternative using likelihood-based criteria. This is a comparison on the available data, rather than a reported test on a separate held-out dataset. Its high-threshold analytical laws also have a different role from finite-threshold simulation: the simulations can examine regimes where those limiting formulas are only approximate.
items.deletion_test: Keep the specific inference limit: fitted-data comparison is not held-out prediction; one cutoff does not describe every panel; sufficient model agreement does not uniquely identify circuitry. Each corrects a likely reading of this evidence.

items.exact_passage: The paper defines its local correlation scale by $\ell=\sqrt{-C(0)/C''(0)}$ in one dimension. The code also uses a parameter called `sigma`, but as the width $b$ of the Gaussian smoothing filter. For ideal continuous white noise smoothed by a Gaussian of width $b$, the covariance is proportional to $\exp[-x^2/(4b^2)]$. Differentiating at zero gives $\ell=\sqrt2\,b$. The two widths are therefore different quantities.
items.deletion_test: This refers backward to the two defined widths or the three cited papers. It does not announce or postpone an unexplained list.
